name: Gemcitabine + Cisplatin (GC)
cyclesNote: Neoadjuvant: 4 cycles (category 1 for MIBC). Metastatic: continued per response/tolerance.

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Cytotoxic gemcitabine/cisplatin backbone is not biomarker-restricted. Applies to urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (#57) and, as the same systemic regimen, upper-tract urothelial carcinoma of the ureter and renal pelvis (#58). Requires cisplatin eligibility (adequate renal function and performance status). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (BL-G).

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration and antiemetics
premedications.notes: vigorous pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration with attention to urine output; high-emetic-risk antiemetic prophylaxis for cisplatin.

supportiveCare: Cisplatin: mandatory vigorous IV hydration (pre and post) to protect renal function; monitor magnesium/potassium and replace.
Antiemetics: cisplatin is highly emetogenic - use a high-emetic-risk prophylaxis regimen.
Monitor for cisplatin nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity (audiometry if symptomatic), and peripheral neuropathy.
CBC before each dose (gemcitabine day 15 is frequently held for cytopenias).
monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each cycle - cisplatin nephrotoxicity

doseModificationRules.text: Reassess cisplatin eligibility if renal function declines; consider split-dose cisplatin (BL-G) or switch to a carboplatin-based regimen. Do not substitute carboplatin for cisplatin in the perioperative setting (BL-G).
Hold gemcitabine day 15 for significant neutropenia/thrombocytopenia per protocol; obtain clinical review.

drugs.name: Gemcitabine
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 17414 (gemcitabine dosing table, bladder cancer) and line 155247 / Table 44.5: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle. NOTE: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G) prefer a 21-day GC schedule (gemcitabine days 1 and 8) for better dose adherence; that variant is recorded in evidence.divergence. The modeled doses are the DeVita 28-day schedule.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 17414 (Bladder cancer: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 d); line 155247 (GC in 28-day cycles, gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15); Table 44.5 (line ~155202)

drugs.name: CISplatin
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 44.5 and line 155247: CISplatin 70 mg/m2 IV on day 2 of the 28-day GC cycle (day 1 is an accepted alternative in 21-day schedules). ISMP tall-man (CISplatin). Requires vigorous IV hydration; monitor for nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy. For borderline renal function, Standard Guidelines (NCCN) BL-G describe a split-dose option (35 mg/m2 on days 1 and 2, or days 1 and 8, category 2B).

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
